title: Counting-sort loop with an invariant
statement: Let $L$ be resource limits, $P$ a program, and $d$ an execution depth. Let $A$ be counting-sort arguments, let $\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be the original memory, let $\sigma$ be an initial state, let $e\in\mathbb{Z}$ be an entry value, let $h$ be an upper-bound expression, let $s$ be a loop body, let $T,m\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $R$ be a predicate on indices and memories. Suppose $\sigma$ satisfies the counting-sort state condition for $A$ at entry value $e$, with invariant $R(0)$. For every $j<m$, all integer counters $c,p$, and every memory $\mu'$ that agrees with $\mu$ outside both the destination interval and the scratch interval and satisfies $R(j)$, suppose the body executes from the state encoded by $A,j,c,p,\mu'$ within the body's block cost and ends in a state satisfying the counting-sort state condition at entry value $j$ with invariant $R(j+1)$. Suppose also that, for every $j\in\mathbb{N}$, all integers $c,p$, and every memory $\mu'$, the expression $h$ is safe in the state encoded by $A,j,c,p,\mu'$ and has value $m$ there; that $m\leq L.word$; and that $m(\operatorname{cost}(h)+\operatorname{blockCost}(s)+7)+\operatorname{cost}(h)+5\leq T$. Then the for-loop with counter variable $8$, upper bound $h$, and body $s$ executes from $\sigma$ within cost $T$ and ends in a state satisfying the counting-sort state condition for $A$ at entry value $m$ with invariant $R(m)$.
